scenarios.title: Fake Out buys one free turn
scenarios.lesson: Fake Out (+3) goes before every normal move, so the target flinches and loses its turn. It works only on the turn the user enters, and Normal-type moves cannot hit Ghosts.
scenarios.assumption: Kingambit is the slowest Pokémon on the field (base Speed 50), so it acts after both of yours. Damage is not simulated.

turns.title: Turn 1: both sides just arrived
turns.prompt: Delphox wants a Nasty Plot. Kingambit threatens it. Where does the Fake Out go?
turns.field: Turn 1. Every Pokémon is new on the field.
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Delphox. Sinistcha: Matcha Gotcha (hits both of yours).

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Kingambit · Delphox: Nasty Plot
happens: Fake Out (+3) resolves before every priority-0 move, so Kingambit flinches and its Kowtow Cleave never happens.
Delphox sets up for free: Special Attack +2.
Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha is resisted by Fire-types.
why: Aim Fake Out at the attacker you fear. Kowtow Cleave is Dark, which hits Psychic-type Delphox for double damage.
The turn Fake Out removes is the value, not its 40 power.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Sinistcha · Delphox: Nasty Plot
happens: Fake Out is Normal-type and Sinistcha is part Ghost, so it does nothing.
The Fake Out is also spent: it only works on the first turn out.
Kowtow Cleave hits Delphox while it sets up.
why: Check the target's typing before you commit Fake Out. Ghost types are immune.
A wasted Fake Out cannot be retried next turn.

options.label: Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit · Delphox: Nasty Plot
happens: Flare Blitz is super effective on Kingambit, but damage only stops the Kowtow Cleave if it knocks Kingambit out first.
Whether it does depends on investment, which this page does not simulate.
why: Fake Out gives certainty: the flinch always stops the attack. Damage gives a chance.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Kingambit · Delphox: Protect

order.note: blocked on Delphox, resisted on Incineroar

happens: Nothing lands on Delphox, but Fake Out had already stopped Kowtow Cleave.
Delphox spent its turn on a Protect it did not need.
why: When Fake Out already handles the threat, Protect is a wasted action and starts your Protect chain.

turns.title: Turn 2: the free turn is spent
turns.prompt: Delphox is at +2 Special Attack. Kingambit is free to move now. What now?
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Delphox. Sinistcha: Matcha Gotcha.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Kingambit
options.disabled: Fake Out only works on the turn its user enters the field. In the Champions ruleset the move is greyed out on later turns.

options.label: Delphox: Heat Wave · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: Delphox cashes in the +2 with a spread move that is super effective on Kingambit (Steel) and on Sinistcha (Grass).
Kingambit is the slowest, so both attacks land before it moves. Whether that is a knockout depends on investment (not simulated).
why: Free setup turns should be spent, not repeated: convert the boost into damage the moment the threat is neutralised.

options.label: Delphox: Nasty Plot · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: The Fake Out is gone, so this Nasty Plot is not free: Kowtow Cleave lands on Delphox.
why: You get one free turn per Fake Out. Greed after that is paid for in damage taken.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: Safe: Kowtow Cleave is blocked. But the +2 sits unused and Protect cannot be repeated next turn.
why: Protect delays the trade rather than winning it.

scenarios.takeaway: Spend Fake Out on the fearsome attacker of the turn you enter, never on a Ghost, then cash the free turn into setup and the setup into damage.

scenarios.title: Protect beats Fake Out, if you guess who
scenarios.lesson: Protect (+4) resolves before Fake Out (+3), but it only covers the Pokémon that used it. A blocked Fake Out is still used up.
scenarios.assumption: Both of the opponent's moves target Blastoise. Damage is not simulated.

turns.title: Turn 1: the opposing Rillaboom is fresh
turns.prompt: Blastoise wants Shell Smash, and Rillaboom's Fake Out is coming. Who do you guard?
turns.field: Turn 1. Every Pokémon is new on the field.
turns.opp_plan: Rillaboom: Fake Out → Blastoise. Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Blastoise.

options.label: Blastoise: Protect · Delphox: Nasty Plot
happens: Protect (+4) resolves before Fake Out (+3): the Fake Out and the Kowtow Cleave both hit a wall.
Rillaboom's Fake Out is used up even though it was blocked. Delphox sets up unharmed.
why: Protect the Pokémon the Fake Out is aimed at, usually the one that wants to set up.
The first turn out is Fake Out's only turn, so blocking it once removes it for good.

options.label: Blastoise: Shell Smash · Delphox: Protect
happens: Fake Out flinches Blastoise before Shell Smash, so the setup fails.
Protect covered Delphox, which was never targeted.
why: Protect covers only the user. Guessing the wrong slot wastes both turns.

options.label: Blastoise: Protect · Delphox: Protect
happens: Nothing lands, but you made no progress and both Protects now face a 1 in 3 chance next turn.
why: Double Protect is a scouting or stalling tool, not a plan. It cannot be repeated.

options.label: Blastoise: Shell Smash · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: Blastoise flinches and gets no boosts, then takes a Kowtow Cleave.
why: Going for setup into a known Fake Out gives the opponent your turn.

turns.title: Turn 2: the Fake Out is spent
turns.prompt: Rillaboom cannot Fake Out again. Blastoise used Protect last turn. What now?
turns.field: Turn 2. Delphox has Sp. Atk +2. Blastoise used Protect last turn.
turns.opp_plan: Rillaboom: Wood Hammer → Delphox. Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Blastoise.

options.label: Blastoise: Shell Smash · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: neutral, on a Blastoise with -1 Def

happens: Shell Smash is not a protecting move, so it also resets the Protect counter.
Delphox spends its +2 on a spread move that is super effective on both foes.
why: With Fake Out gone, this is the safe window for setup.

options.label: Blastoise: Protect (again) · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: 2 in 3 chance: second use in a row

branches.text: Protect works: Kowtow Cleave is blocked. The chain then drops to 1 in 9 next turn.

happens: Protect used twice in a row succeeds only 1 time in 3.
Most of the time you get nothing and lose the setup window.
why: The window is free, so spend it on setup instead of a coin flip.

options.label: Blastoise: Water Spout · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: A perfectly good attack, but Water Spout is resisted by Grass and neutral on Kingambit.
why: You could attack now, but the boost from Shell Smash pays off across later turns.

scenarios.takeaway: Protect the slot the Fake Out is aimed at. The Fake Out is then gone for good, and the next turn belongs to your setup.

scenarios.title: Quick Guard covers both partners
scenarios.lesson: Quick Guard blocks every priority move aimed at your side while both of your Pokémon act. It has the same +3 priority as Fake Out, so the faster Pokémon acts first.
scenarios.assumption: Sneasler is faster than Rillaboom. If Rillaboom were faster, its Fake Out would resolve first and Quick Guard would be too late.

turns.title: Turn 1: two priority threats
turns.prompt: Rillaboom Fake Outs Delphox and Kingambit Sucker Punches it too. Delphox wants to attack this turn. One move stops both.
turns.field: Turn 1. Every Pokémon is new on the field.
turns.opp_plan: Rillaboom: Fake Out → Delphox. Kingambit: Sucker Punch → Delphox.

options.label: Sneasler: Quick Guard · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: Quick Guard goes up first (+3, faster than Rillaboom) and blocks Fake Out (+3) and Sucker Punch (+1).
Delphox is untouched and still gets to attack.
why: Protect on Delphox would also block both, but then Delphox does nothing. Quick Guard lets it act.
It only works if it resolves first: a faster Fake Out beats it.

options.label: Sneasler: Fake Out → Rillaboom · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: The faster Fake Out flinches Rillaboom, so its own Fake Out never happens.
But Sucker Punch (+1) still hits Delphox first, super effectively, and Delphox may not survive to Heat Wave.
why: A flinch answers one priority move. Quick Guard answers both.

options.label: Sneasler: Protect · Delphox: Heat Wave
options.disabled: Tang's Sneasler carries Fake Out, Close Combat, Poison Jab and Quick Guard, not Protect.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Sneasler: Close Combat → Kingambit
happens: Protect stops both, and Sneasler's Close Combat is 4x on Kingambit.
But Delphox spent its turn on Protect, and this only works because both attacks were aimed at Delphox.
why: Protect covers one slot. If the Fake Out had been aimed at Sneasler instead, this line would fail.

scenarios.takeaway: Quick Guard turns two priority threats into one answer and lets both partners act, but only when your Quick Guard user is faster than their Fake Out user.

scenarios.title: Protect to scout, and to blank Sucker Punch
scenarios.lesson: A Protect turn costs an attack but shows the opponent's hand. Sucker Punch also fails into any status move.
scenarios.assumption: Sinistcha's fourth move is unknown to you at team preview. Here it turns out to be Trick Room.

turns.title: Turn 1: what does Sinistcha run?
turns.prompt: You know Kingambit likes Sucker Punch. You do not know Sinistcha's moves. Do you attack, or learn something?
turns.field: Turn 1. Every Pokémon is new on the field.
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Sucker Punch → Delphox. Sinistcha: Trick Room.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Blastoise: Shell Smash
happens: Sucker Punch (+1) goes first and fails, because Protect is a status move.
Sinistcha reveals Trick Room, which resolves last at -7 priority.
Blastoise's +2 Speed now points the wrong way: under Trick Room slower is faster.
why: Protect turned Delphox's turn into information and a whiffed Sucker Punch.
Knowing about Trick Room changes how you value speed boosts next turn.

options.label: Delphox: Heat Wave · Blastoise: Shell Smash
happens: Sucker Punch (+1) hits Delphox before it acts, and Delphox may not survive to use Heat Wave.
why: Attacking into a priority move gives up the turn.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Blastoise: Protect
happens: You see everything and take nothing, but you did nothing and now cannot Protect reliably next turn.
why: One Protect scouts. Two Protects are just a delay.

options.label: Delphox: Nasty Plot · Blastoise: Protect

order.note: Nasty Plot is a status move

happens: Sucker Punch also fails into Nasty Plot, so Delphox is fine here and gains +2.
why: This works only because Kingambit chose Sucker Punch. Had it used Kowtow Cleave, Delphox would take a super-effective hit. Protect covers every attack.

scenarios.takeaway: Protect is an information tool as much as a defensive one. Use it on the turn the opponent's plan matters most and read what they reveal.

scenarios.title: Protect stalls one turn, not five
scenarios.lesson: Protect works every time the first time, then only 1 in 3, then 1 in 9. Any other action resets the chain. Champions also cuts Protect to 8 PP.
scenarios.assumption: Trick Room lasts 5 turns and reverses order within a priority bracket, so Kingambit moves before Delphox. Damage is not simulated.

turns.title: Turn 2 of 5: Trick Room is up
turns.prompt: Trick Room was just set. Delphox is now slower than Kingambit. Stall with Protect?
turns.field: Trick Room: turn 2 of 5. Protect chain: 0.
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Delphox. Sinistcha: Matcha Gotcha.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit

order.note: blocked on Delphox, resisted on Incineroar

happens: The first Protect always succeeds and Kowtow Cleave is blocked.
Three Trick Room turns remain after this one.
why: Protect is the right first move: it buys a turn of Trick Room for free.

options.label: Delphox: Heat Wave · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: Under Trick Room Kingambit acts first, so Delphox eats a super-effective hit before it moves.
why: A fast Pokémon under Trick Room is the slow one. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave never misses.

options.label: Delphox: Protect · Incineroar: Parting Shot → Sinistcha, switch to Blastoise

order.note: Atk and Sp. Atk -1; Incineroar switches out
-1 Sp. Atk; hits Blastoise super effectively

happens: Delphox is safe and Sinistcha's Special Attack drops, but Blastoise switches into a super-effective Matcha Gotcha.
why: A pivot is only as good as the Pokémon it brings in. Grass hits Water hard, so this switch-in is poor.

turns.title: Turn 3 of 5: Protect again?
turns.prompt: Delphox used Protect last turn. Trick Room has 3 turns left. Do you repeat it?
turns.field: Trick Room: turn 3 of 5. Protect chain: 1.
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Delphox. Sinistcha: Matcha Gotcha.

options.label: Delphox: Protect (again) · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit

order.note: 2 in 3 chance: second use in a row

branches.text: Protect works: Kowtow Cleave is blocked. The next attempt would be 1 in 9, with two Trick Room turns still left.

happens: Protect used twice in a row succeeds only 1 time in 3.
Even when it works you are 1 in 9 the turn after.
why: You cannot outlast a 5-turn Trick Room with Protect. Plan the second turn now.

options.label: Delphox: switch → Blastoise · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: Switching moves the hit onto a Pokémon that takes it neutrally, and it resets the Protect chain.
Blastoise takes Matcha Gotcha super effectively, so this is not free.
why: Protect for one turn, then switch: it burns two Trick Room turns instead of gambling on the second.

options.label: Delphox: Heat Wave · Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit
happens: Delphox is still slower than Kingambit under Trick Room.
why: Attacking into a faster (under Trick Room) opponent is the same mistake as before.

scenarios.takeaway: Protect stalls one turn: 100%, then 33%, then 11%. Use it once, then switch or attack, and remember the chain resets after any other action.

scenarios.title: Parting Shot: debuff and reposition in one action
scenarios.lesson: A pivot attacks or debuffs and switches in one action, so the incoming Pokémon absorbs the hit meant for the one that left.
scenarios.assumption: Trick Room is up, so the slower Incineroar acts before Sneasler and Rillaboom. Damage is not simulated.

turns.title: Turn 1: Incineroar is the target
turns.prompt: Sneasler's Close Combat (double damage on Incineroar) and Rillaboom's Wood Hammer are both aimed at Incineroar. Delphox waits in the back.
turns.field: Trick Room is up. Incineroar acts first.
turns.opp_plan: Sneasler: Close Combat → Incineroar. Rillaboom: Wood Hammer → Incineroar.

options.label: Incineroar: Parting Shot → Sneasler, switch to Delphox · Blastoise: Shell Smash

order.note: Atk and Sp. Atk -1, then Incineroar leaves

happens: Sneasler's Attack is lowered before it swings.
Delphox switches in and takes both attacks, resisting Fighting and Grass.
Incineroar is preserved and can return to Intimidate again later.
why: A pivot is two actions in one: a debuff now and a better matchup for the hits already incoming.
Aim the drop at the Pokémon that will hurt you most.

options.label: Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Rillaboom · Blastoise: Shell Smash
happens: Incineroar stays in and takes a super-effective Close Combat.
why: Staying in against the hit you know is coming costs HP a pivot would have saved.

options.label: Incineroar: switch → Delphox · Blastoise: Shell Smash
happens: Same positioning as Parting Shot, but Sneasler keeps full Attack.
why: When Parting Shot can connect, it does everything a plain switch does plus a debuff.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Sneasler · Blastoise: Shell Smash
options.disabled: Fake Out only works on the turn its user enters the field, and Incineroar has been out.

scenarios.takeaway: Parting Shot debuffs the attacker and puts a resist in front of the hit, in one action. Use it when the hit is already coming.

scenarios.title: A pivot only works if it connects
scenarios.lesson: Parting Shot is blocked by Protect, and into Defiant it can raise Attack instead of lowering it. A blocked pivot also cancels the switch.
scenarios.assumption: Kingambit's ability is Defiant. Rillaboom's moves are as stated. Damage is not simulated.

turns.title: Turn 1: which target?
turns.prompt: Incineroar wants to pivot into Blastoise. Two targets: Kingambit or Rillaboom.
turns.field: Turn 1. Incineroar has been out for a while.
turns.opp_plan: Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Incineroar. Rillaboom: Wood Hammer → Delphox.

options.label: Incineroar: Parting Shot → Rillaboom, switch to Blastoise · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: Atk and Sp. Atk -1, then Incineroar leaves

happens: Parting Shot connects: Rillaboom's Wood Hammer weakens and Incineroar leaves.
Blastoise takes Kowtow Cleave neutrally instead of Incineroar taking it.
why: Choose the pivot target that does not punish stat drops.

options.label: Incineroar: Parting Shot → Kingambit, switch to Blastoise · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: Defiant raises Attack by 2 whenever its stats are lowered, so Kingambit ends up with more Attack than before.
Blastoise now takes a boosted Kowtow Cleave.
why: Never lower the stats of a Defiant Pokémon unless you want it stronger.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Kingambit · Delphox: Heat Wave
options.disabled: Fake Out only works on the turn its user enters the field, and Incineroar has been out.

turns.title: Turn 2: the opponent protects
turns.prompt: Incineroar just switched back in. Rillaboom will Protect. Kingambit will Kowtow Cleave. Which move connects?
turns.field: Turn 2. Incineroar just switched back in, so Fake Out is available again.
turns.opp_plan: Rillaboom: Protect. Kingambit: Kowtow Cleave → Delphox.

options.label: Incineroar: Parting Shot → Rillaboom · Delphox: Heat Wave
happens: Protect blocks Parting Shot, so nothing is lowered and Incineroar does not switch.
Delphox still eats Kowtow Cleave.
why: The switch is part of the move: if the move is blocked, so is the pivot.

options.label: Incineroar: Fake Out → Kingambit · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: blocked on Rillaboom, super effective on Kingambit

happens: Switching Incineroar back in re-arms Fake Out: it flinches Kingambit, so Kowtow Cleave never happens.
Rillaboom's Protect only blocks what is aimed at it, so Heat Wave still hits Kingambit.
why: A pivot that comes back in resets Fake Out. Pivoting and Fake Out work as a cycle.
Against a Protect, aim at the Pokémon that is not protecting.

options.label: Incineroar: Flare Blitz → Kingambit · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: blocked on Rillaboom, super effective on Kingambit

happens: Both attacks land on Kingambit, but it can still Kowtow Cleave Delphox if it survives.
why: Fake Out would have made that Kowtow Cleave certain not to happen.

options.label: Incineroar: Parting Shot → Kingambit · Delphox: Heat Wave

order.note: blocked on Rillaboom, super effective on Kingambit

happens: Parting Shot connects but Defiant turns it into an Attack boost for Kingambit.
why: The same Defiant trap as turn 1.

scenarios.takeaway: Before you pivot, check three things: is the target protecting, does its ability punish stat drops, and does the switch-in take the coming hit well.
